open_points.subject: sandbox scratch-limit outcome when SIGXFSZ uses its default disposition
open_points.text: “a limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, `output_bytes`) — `resource_exhausted`” contradicts “Code that restores the signal's default and is killed by it exited abnormally (`crashed`)”
open_points.question: When a write exceeds the scratch file-size limit after code restores the signal's default and SIGXFSZ kills the process, is the execution `resource_exhausted` under the outcome precedence or `crashed` under the new exception?
open_points.default_guess: `crashed`, treating the new specific sentence as an exception to the general precedence rule

open_points.subject: sandbox detection of a caught scratch-limit write error
open_points.text: “the runner ignores the signal the host sends for a write past it, so the write fails with an error the code can see” and “Only that error is a scratch hit”
open_points.question: If user code catches the write-past-limit error and returns conforming outputs, must the execution still be `resource_exhausted`, and if so what observable event tells the runner or parent that the caught error occurred while the signal is ignored?
options: Any write-past-limit error is recorded and forces `resource_exhausted`, even when caught
Only an uncaught write-past-limit error forces `resource_exhausted`; a caught one may succeed
A caught error is entirely the code's concern
open_points.default_guess: Any write-past-limit error forces `resource_exhausted`, with the runner required to record the event through a mechanism not yet specified

open_points.subject: classification of host-storage write failures
open_points.text: “a write that fails because host storage is exhausted is an ordinary raised error (`crashed` if it escapes `run`)”
open_points.question: Which concrete write failures count as “host storage is exhausted,” and does this rule cover only writes performed by `run` or also module loading and runner/exchange-directory writes?
options: Only `ENOSPC` raised by a write performed during `run`
`ENOSPC` and quota exhaustion such as `EDQUOT` during `run`
Any capacity-related failure anywhere in sandbox setup, module loading, execution, or output collection
open_points.default_guess: Treat `ENOSPC` and `EDQUOT` from user-code writes during `run` as ordinary exceptions; failures in sandbox setup or runner output handling are `crashed`

open_points.subject: short or partial writes at the scratch limit
open_points.text: “a limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, `output_bytes`) — `resource_exhausted`” conflicts with “a short or partial write is the code's own concern” and “Only that error is a scratch hit”
open_points.question: If the kernel enforces the file-size limit by returning a short or partial write without a separate write error, has the scratch limit been hit for outcome classification, or may the execution still succeed if `run` returns conforming outputs?
options: The execution is `resource_exhausted` because the limit was reached
The partial write alone is not a scratch hit and the execution may succeed
The result depends on whether a later write produces the limit error
open_points.default_guess: The partial write alone does not force `resource_exhausted`; only a subsequent explicit write-past-limit error does
